Thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is a short private-offer summary and an updated SOW (medisys_sow_v2.pdf). Hi Jane —

Appreciate the clarity. We can do a 24-month committed private offer and offer a blended discount on the committed tiers. High level options:

A) 24-month upfront commit: larger one-time credit, lowest effective rate (need legal to sign standard AWS PO doc).
B) 24-month split billing (BU A / BU B): we can structure two linked private offers; requires both BU legal/procurement signatures and AWS gating on buyer eligibility.
C) 24-month monthly invoicing: slightly higher effective rate than upfront commit but spreads cash impact.

I'll attach a draft where we flag billing cadence options. For SOC2/evidence we maintain a summary PDF — Naomi, please include the evidence-pack link in the PO submission.

Hi all —

Two technical notes on the AWS Marketplace private-offer flow to set expectations:

1) Approval windows: once we create the private offer in the Seller Console, the buyer has a configurable signature window (we generally set 30 days). If you need >30 days we can request a longer window but AWS can require seller-side approvals.

2) Multi-account / split billing: AWS allows linking offers but each buyer account must accept individually. For MediSys multi-BU this means procurement + BU signers for each account; activation only proceeds after the last account accepts.

I'll prepare a PO draft aligned to option B (linked offers) and include a suggested DocuSign envelope to speed CFO signature. I've attached the PO template with the AWS-specific metadata filled (po-draft-terms.docx).

—Karthik
